title: Re-examine exits after combat-forced relocation
root_cause_hypothesis: The origin is decision_logic: the east move IS productive (it lands the agent in a new room, 'huge pile of garbage'), so no existing guard misfires — but determine_next_action has no rule to re-look/re-examine exits of a room after an unexpected combat-triggered relocation, and no such re-examination trigger exists today.
change_summary: The 'east' exit from 'dingy stable' is a real, productive move (it deposits the agent in a genuinely new room via a combat interlude), so futile-edge marking and loop-break logic are contraindicated and would wrongly discard a valid route. The real gap is that determine_next_action never revisits/re-examines the origin room's exit set after a forced relocation, so alternative exits from the stable are never explored. Add a selection-policy trigger: when a move's landing room differs from any Unknown-exit target the agent was navigating toward (i.e. a forced/unexpected relocation), set a flag so the next action re-looks at the room and re-scans its exits, rather than treating the destination as a normal frontier. This changes only priority ordering / navigation scoring, not any edge's futile state.
acceptance_criteria: In a future run log, after 'east' from 'dingy stable' lands the agent in 'huge pile of garbage', a subsequent step issues a 'look' or re-examines the stable's remaining Unknown exits (visible in the action/reason fields).
No edge from 'dingy stable' (including 'east') is marked futile in knight_orc_strategy.json as a result of this relocation.
The stable's non-east Unknown exits are eventually explored (new exploration edges appear in the world_graph rather than the agent repeatedly re-taking east).
risk_notes: Must not trigger the re-look flag on ordinary successful moves (would waste turns on 'look'); scope the trigger narrowly to relocations that diverge from the intended navigation target or that co-occur with a combat/interlude marker. Watch for interaction with position_lost handling so the two flags don't cause redundant consecutive 'look' actions. Ensure no LLM call is added to the hot path — detection must be from existing extracted state diffs only.
fixed_in: PR #82 — the proposed re-look trigger was unnecessary: position_lost already forces a look on the very next step whenever a direction move succeeds with no extracted room (which is exactly what happened here), and the log confirms that look correctly re-examined the room and reported its real exits. The actual bug was one step earlier and more precise: when that same step (the 'east' move) reported exits without a room (extract_knowledge dropped the room field but kept 'Exits: down, outside' from the combat-interlude text), process_agent_step still called update_graph(state, state['current_room'], exits, ...) — but state['current_room'] was still the *old* room (nothing updates it when extracted.room is falsy), so 'huge pile of garbage's real exits got wired as phantom Unknown edges hanging off 'dingy stable', which does not actually have them (its only real exit is 'east'). This is also the origin of the bogus 'down'/'out' edges that fed P005/P006. Fixed by skipping update_graph entirely for the one step where a directional move sets position_lost (exits reported that step belong to the room just entered, not the stale current_room) — the follow-up forced look already re-reports the same exits correctly attributed once the room resolves, so nothing is lost, only the earlier mis-attribution is prevented.
